text:
marta: running intermittent-surge sims for Dedicated clusters across eu-west / us-central. attached perf traces and CSV in the sheet: https://go/reports/ded-surge-2196 :chart_with_upwards_trend: Need help picking per-GPU concurrency targets.

ajay: quick q — what's the p99 SLO here? are we optimizing cost or strict latency? :thinking:

marta: SLO = p99 <= 220ms for ~2k token median requests. cost goal <= $0.003/token. can relax to 300ms for background batchy routes.

benji: from sims: h100-80g sustains ~13 concurrent @2k tokens using XLA-optim kernels, a100-40g ~8 with fused kernels. p99 tails when utilization > 90%. suggest per-GPU conc targets: h100=10, a100=6 (keep ~20% headroom).

kevin: can we add per-region fallback? e.g., if eu surge saturates, route to quant-8bit variant or to cached short-response path?

marta: yes. plan: primary -> quant-8bit-ptq variant during surge. if latency > 400ms then fallback to cached-short path. enable KV-prefix caching for chat sessions to cut repeated tokens.

dani: autoscale note — sims assumed instant spin-up of 2 nodes. reality: spin-up ~2.5min. recommend warm pool of 15% of expected peak and autoscale increments of 1 node with cooldown 90s.

ajay: warm pool 15% + 20% buffer = 35% reserved which increases cost. alternative: warm 10% + shared reserved burst 30% from a cross-region reserve. can you re-run sims with that policy?

marta: re-ran with warm 10% + reserved shared burst 30% + targets h100=10,a100=6. results: eu p99 ~210ms, us p99 ~235ms. cost delta +7% vs baseline. artifacts: charts + CSV in sheet.

sre-bot: sim-run 2196543210 complete — artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-sims/dedicated/2196543210.tar.gz

benji: kernel note: fused-kernel yields better median but worse p99 under micro-bursts. XLA-optim is more stable for tail. for quant-8bit, fused-kernel adds dequant overhead that hurts micro-burst p99.

kevin: next steps: A) adopt h100 conc=10, a100 conc=6 B) config warm_pool_pct=10 + reserved_burst_pct=30 C) canary in one region for 48h D) rollback via model-variant fallback ready. who owns rollout?

marta: I'll own rollout + canary. tagging @kevin for infra CI. PR will include runtime config snippet and dashboards. plan canary start: Tue 06:00 UTC.

marta: config snippet for ops repo:```
gpu_targets:
  h100: 10
  a100: 6
warm_pool_pct: 10
reserved_burst_pct: 30
canary_duration_hours: 48
```

kevin: sounds good. please include explicit alert thresholds for model-variant fallback (p99 > 300ms for 5m) and checkout the KV cache hitrate dashboard before canary.

marta: will do. leaving action items in the thread and PR. :white_check_mark:
